text:
Boston paid two first-round picks to get JJ Peterka from Utah in June, and the early returns look like a player who needed a bigger role. He is playing 17:38 a night, up from 15:59 last season, and has 14 points in 19 games. More telling, his own chances are up to 1.15 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his shots), from 0.73.

This is one of the cleaner breakouts on the board. His shooting is a little under our range, so the 5 goals, if anything, undersell the chances. The Bruins have finished about three goals better than expected with him on the ice, which flatters the assists some, but at five on five they are winning the chance battle with him out there (55% of expected goals).

His speed is the thing you notice: 62 bursts over 20 miles per hour already, 97th percentile in the league. His goal against Florida, which NHL.com clipped as "Pastrnak sets up Peterka," is the version of him the trade was made for. Evolving-Hockey noted he was better than his goals last season too; watch whether the finishing finally catches up to the chances.
